correctness.rationale: For a nontrivial Cartesian product of connected simple factors, a crossing edge in one coordinate uses the unique external-neighbor budget at both endpoints; every perpendicular edge becomes monochromatic, forcing parallel crossing through each square. Propagation across connected factors makes every fiber in other coordinates monochromatic and yields a unique active coordinate. A factor crossing edge lifts to N_i edges, so F_product(u,v)=sum_i F_factor_i(u,v^{N_i}). For P_n each matching of t crossing edges has binom(n-t,t) locations and yields t+1 consecutive constant runs; proper unordered k-partitions of the run path are Stirling S(t,k-1). For C_n cyclic matching locations are n/(n-t)*binom(n-t,t) and the proper run-cycle color partitions give the inclusion-exclusion chromatic polynomial q_t(k). Independent separate enumeration of restricted-growth partitions of P2..P7, C3..C7, and products P2 square P3, P3 square P3, C3 square P2 matched complete (k,t) distributions. Explicitly t>=2 for cycles and C3 has zero multicuts. Packaged check_matching_multicuts.py source inspected; finite cases do not establish arbitrary factors.
